meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

"The zero stands." On what basis, Hale, because your own procedure says you call the parent before any mark goes in, and nobody called me. Show me what you have, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
I'm writing down October 15. Show me both, Hale: the line in the essay, and the outline with his name and that date on it. An outline is a plan, and students change their minds.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone called me, and copies of the essay line and the October 15 outline you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the documents for herself.
What moved her: "the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet" and the dated outline, because they were specific, tied to Owen's work and checkable, which got her writing and asking for the papers.
What cost ground: "The zero stands." because it refused any basis and sounded like deciding first, which pushed her straight to the principal.
Try next time: in your first line, own that the zero went in before you called home, then put the October 15 outline and the essay line in front of her to read herself.
